$schema-note: THE ENUMERATION #565 ASKED FOR, as a committed artifact rather than prose.
A label-dependent check is one whose BEHAVIOUR branches on a pull-request
label. Every such check inherits the label-blind sampling rule: a PR is
CREATED by one API call and LABELLED by a separate one, so the `opened` run
is dispatched before the label exists (measured on PR #555: run created
16:10:42Z, `ci:cheap` applied 16:10:43Z). Anything gated on a label is
therefore exercised only on PRs that get pushed to at least twice, unless it
This file is NOT documentation. `check-label-dependence.mjs` compares it
against the tree in BOTH directions: a label-dependent site that is not
declared here fails, and an entry here whose file has stopped being
label-dependent fails too. The second direction is the one that decays,
because an entry nobody compares still READS as though it were guarded.
When the population grows, add the entry AND say how the new check avoids
being verified only by accident of review history.

checks.label: ci:cheap
checks.behaviour: Check E refuses a PR labelled `ci:cheap` whose changed paths trip any filter in test.yml. The lane gate exempts `ci:cheap` PRs from the sequential-PR capacity check, so a mislabelled one consumes a signing-runner slot the gate believes is free.
checks.sampling: SELF-DECLARING. On an `opened` payload an absent `ci:cheap` is not authoritative, so the run computes the tripped filters anyway and announces that classification is DEFERRED, naming them. It exits 0 rather than 2 because exit 2 in the PR path reddens every PR at creation; the claim is deferred, not abandoned, and lane-check.yml checks it. An unreadable payload is CANNOT CHECK (exit 2), never a pass.

checks.label: ci:cheap
checks.behaviour: Runs check-path-filters.mjs on the `labeled` event, when the PR's current label set contains `ci:cheap`, so the lane claim is verified with the label demonstrably present instead of depending on whether someone pushed twice.
checks.sampling: THIS CHECK IS ITSELF LABEL-DEPENDENT, and that is the honest reading: the fix for the sampling rule is a check gated on a label. Its gate reads `github.event.pull_request.labels`, the SAME field check-path-filters.mjs parses — not `github.event.label.name`, the single label that triggered the event. Reading the triggering label meant a PR already carrying `ci:cheap` and then given any other label skipped entirely, suppressing a real finding. The identity of those two fields is asserted by check-path-filters.test.mjs.
